title: Provider pinning and semantic-compatibility playbook for Private VPC Terraform upgrades
creator: Sofia Nguyen
body:
Summary:
We need a single-source playbook that documents recommended provider and module pinning, semantic-compatibility signaling, and automated compatibility checks for Private (VPC) Terraform deployments. Goal is to reduce upgrade rollbacks, speed safe upgrades, and provide clear remediation guidance for infra engineers and SREs when provider/module updates are incompatible with our VPC modules.

Problem statement:
- Multiple private VPC customers run pinned provider/module versions; some pin to older providers to maintain runtime stability. We lack a reproducible compatibility matrix and an automation layer that: (1) asserts compatibility before upgrades, (2) surfaces breaking changes affecting our modules, and (3) automatically generates canary plans and rollbacks for Dedicated/Private upgrades.

Scope / non-goals:
- IN SCOPE: Terraform providers used by our private VPC modules (aws, awscc, google, azurerm), our internal module catalog, CI preflight checks, documentation, and automated drift/health probes.
- NOT SCOPE: Customer-managed modules outside our curated catalog, cloud account-level provider policies (these are advisory).

Proposal / deliverables:
1) Compatibility signaller: a single YAML/JSON artifact per module that declares the minimal supported provider version range and known incompatibilities with explicit upgrade notes and migration steps.
2) Pinbook: an opinionated canonical list of provider and module pins per supported private-VPC release and a recommended upgrade cadence (major/minor policy).
3) Preflight CI job: terraform-compat-check that runs in PRs targeting module or provider bumps; it runs a matrix of plan/apply with mocked inputs and asserts known postconditions (resource changes, schema diffs).
4) Canary upgrade playbook: automated runbook that executes in a staging slice (subset of accounts) and captures health signals (provisioning success, instance metadata drift, route tables, subnet allocations).
5) Observability hooks: new console dashboard panel and Log/Tracing tags for pin-related rollouts and automated alerts when preflight checks change status.

Acceptance criteria:
- A machine-readable compatibility artifact exists for each VPC module in modules/vpc/ with the following fields: supported_providers, min_compatible_versions, incompatible_changes, migration_steps (short).
- CI job blocks merges for provider bumps that have unknown/incompatible diffs unless triaged and an exception is documented.
- Playbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step canary/rollback and one tested runbook executed in staging.
- Telemetry: new metric provider.pin_check.failures with dashboard and alert (SLO: <1 failure per month in canary runs, otherwise P1 page).

Technical approach / decisions to make:
- Pin format: propose semver ranges using plugin constraints (e.g. >= 4.20.0, < 5.0.0) stored alongside module metadata. Tradeoff: strict ranges reduce risk but increase maintenance overhead.
- Compatibility detection: combine terraform plan diffs with provider schema diffs using the terraform providers schema extractor (community tool) + custom heuristics for resource-level breaking changes.
- Storage: compatibility artifacts live in the repo next to modules and published to an internal registry for the CI jobs.
- Rollout: staged canary first (5% of accounts), expand via canary automation, with automated rollback on health signal breach.

Risks & mitigations:
- False positives in compatibility detection: mitigate by adding a triage flag and a human-in-the-loop approval step for initial rollouts.
- Maintenance overhead: add a monthly sweep automation that checks upstream provider changelogs and flags modules that may be affected.
- Customer-specific overrides: provide a per-customer override registry but require a signed justification and support plan for extended pins.

Next steps (short-term):
- Week 1: Draft compatibility artifact schema and add example for modules/vpc/networking. (Owner: Marcelo)
- Week 2: Implement initial CI preflight job prototype and wire into module PRs. (Owner: Infra CI team)
- Week 3: Run an internal canary upgrade of aws provider minor bump against staging accounts. Capture telemetry and update playbook. (Owner: SRE + Infra)

Related artifacts:
- PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/xxxx (placeholder for the terraform-compat-check job)
- Confluence playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/VPC+Upgrade+Playbook
- Example compatibility artifact: repo://modules/vpc/networking/compatibility-2025-11.yml

Longer-term ideas:
- Automated changelog monitoring for provider repos with ML-assisted change classification (breaking/behavioral/benign).
- A small service to auto-generate migration snippets when a provider schema change is detected.
comments: 2025-11-14 - Marcelo: Created initial artifact schema draft and pushed example to repo under modules/vpc/networking/compatibility-2025-11.yml. Waiting on feedback from SRE on health signal thresholds.
2025-11-19 - Sofia: Reviewed schema, suggested adding a customer_override section and an expiration_date for overrides. Filed a follow-up task ENG-94045 to track overrides implementation.

2025-11-26 - Marcelo: Prototype CI job (terraform-compat-check) added to infra/.github/workflows/compat-check.yml. It runs in PRs and posts a verdict as a comment. Found two false positives in resource rename scenarios; added a heuristic to detect rename markers.

2025-12-02 - Priya Shah (SRE): Ran staging canary for aws provider 4.28 -> 4.29 against staging slice. Observed route table diff that was expected and safe; flagged a corner-case with subnet tagging behavior that requires a migration step. Added migration snippet to compatibility artifact.
2025-12-05 - Marcelo: Updated acceptance criteria with telemetry metric and added alert runbook link. Scheduling playbook review session with PM and Security for 2025-12-08.
2025-12-05 - Security (notes): security_review_required=true; must validate provider plugin upgrade doesn't introduce new network/credentials flows. Assigned security checklist to ENG-94110.
